status: Complete original h/v complex64 source sampling and paired primary, proper motion, rigid/internal and whole-complex geometry comparisons with released PVB
variant: Frozen original A1 h/v generator, source and decoder; no complex fine-tuning, source retuning, projection or additional sampling guidance
comparison: Same complete atom inventories, windows, future times and evaluation definitions. PVB nativeH1 versus h/v H4, different training/pretraining and NFE; not an equal-budget state-only causal ablation.
delta_convention: h/v minus PVB; arrays give mean and paired95percent system-bootstrap endpoints; listed errors/scores lower is better

proper_motion_followup.interpretation: RMSF-distribution errors remain worse under proper ensemble scoring; MSD-curve scores are worse on all64 but unresolved on new48. Preserve the favorable new48 center-increment path score: the center-path benefit cannot simply be dismissed as absent in temporal increments. The all64 increment interval crosses zero. None repairs the ligand bond deficit or establishes full-joint dynamics.
proper_motion_followup.limitations: Supplementary analysis after primary comparison; finite-window RMSF is not equilibrium RMSF; one MD future per condition, eight draws, marginal paired-system intervals and differing native input/training exposure

rigid_internal_motion_followup.coverage: All128 conditions and1024 cached forecasts per model; zero new neural calls, no coordinate changes or exclusions
rigid_internal_motion_followup.definition: Protein-reference alignment followed by a diagnostic best proper rigid rotation between consecutive ligand frames, fixed atom identities; includes observed-to-first-future step. Internal residual also includes legitimate torsions and deformations, not exclusively bond jitter. Translation is heavy-atom centroid, not mass-weighted COM.
rigid_internal_motion_followup.paired_error_definition: For each system, first average its two condition amplitudes; then compute abs(hv-MD)-abs(PVB-MD). Apply existing system_estimate to these paired system differences. Arrays are mean,95percent bootstrap lower,upper. This is a descriptive amplitude error, not a proper predictive score or a kinetic observable.
rigid_internal_motion_followup.interpretation: Strong excess internal-shape motion coexists with the h/v bond deficit and favorable center-path/increment scores. This supports investigating internally coordinated geometry, not merely increasing global motion amplitude or freezing all atoms. Translation/rotation amplitude-error differences remain unresolved. It does not isolate latent-state causality or demonstrate that coordinate A/B resolves the problem.
rigid_internal_motion_followup.limitations: Posthoc reused-development diagnostic; rotation/residual squared norms have a nonzero cross term and are not additive energy fractions. No ligand symmetry remapping; near-collinear rotation ambiguity is reported in the raw result. One MD future is not an equilibrium reference distribution.

interpretation: The original generic-atom h/v transfer baseline has a large ligand covalent-geometry deficit and larger RMSF error than released PVB on both all64 and new48.

Retain the counterevidence: ligand center-path energy score is better for h/v on both strata, and new48 residue-contact occupancy error improves. These do not compensate for distorted internal geometry or establish correct full dynamics.
MSD and pocket-distance path differences remain unresolved on new48; do not summarize every motion observable as worse.

A/B must improve geometry and motion together. Beating this un-finetuned transfer baseline alone does not prove that h/v stochastic state is intrinsically inferior: architecture, training exposure, pretraining and NFE remain confounded.
No coordinate A/B trained-generation result is yet available; do not interpret these baseline results as evidence for either A or B.

whole_complex_geometry.status: completed all128 conditions; paired all/old16/new48 comparisons completed
whole_complex_geometry.interpretation: The geometry deficit is not confined to ligand bonds: protein bonds and whole-complex clashes are also worse. Scores use the unchanged legacy clash rule on all atoms without projection or relaxation. MD zero clashes under this rule is not proof of perfect force-field geometry. Native inputs and training resources remain confounded.
